text:
incidents-bot: PAGER: high rate of 429s for tenant 'Cedar' (enterprise/vpc) on dedicated-pool cedar-prod-d1. Alerting since 2165432095. Severity: P1.

Jay (oncall): taking. pinging @Alex and @Maria. any customer reports yet?

Alex (sre): seeing a sustained spike in 429s from CID cedar-prod-d1. 429s correlate with token_timeout and queue_overflow in runtime logs.

Alex (sre): quick log sample:```
2026-03-12T02:15:22Z cedar/pool-d1 handle_request failed status=429 reason=queue_overflow qsize=128 max_q=100
2026-03-12T02:15:23Z cedar/pool-d1 kv_hit=false pending=230
```

Maria (support): Cedar reports their nightly batch failing ~02:14-02:20 UTC. They're getting callback retries and partial failures. Customer SLA: enterprise platinum. Ryan (acct) looped in.

Ryan (acct): Cedar is on a reserved capacity contract with burst clauses. They are impacted; they're in the middle of a critical ingest. Please advise on emergency lift options.

Lina (eng-runtime): initial root looks like unexpected request fanout from Cedar's new job pattern + cache miss storm. Dedicated pool reached configured max inflight and backpressure -> 429. Options: 1) temporary emergency burst (raise inflight cap on pool), 2) divert tenant to warm fallback pool, 3) request client-side throttling.

Sam (infra): I can open emergency burst if we get sign-off from Billing & SRE. cost hit is non-trivial. I can also spin up a warm fallback if runtime has capacity.

Jay (oncall): priority: reduce customer impact now. Lina, can you confirm whether fallback pool cedar-warm exists and is compatible (model/quantization)?

Lina (eng-runtime): cedar-warm exists with compatible model v2-q4. KV cache warmup will cause cold misses but should accept traffic. Minor quality diff (edge cases).

Alex (sre): I'll throttle at ingress for Cedar to smooth the spike and open a diversion to cedar-warm. Applying short-term request queuing on edge for tenant id=cedar-tenant-11.

Alex (sre): Applying diversion now:```bash
# runtime-admin (internal)
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/run/divert" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"cedar-tenant-11","from_pool":"cedar-prod-d1","to_pool":"cedar-warm","duration_minutes":30}'
```

incidents-bot: diversion request accepted, job id=div-98342, started 2165432178.

Sam (infra): provisioning emergency burst capacity now as a safety net. Estimated additional GPUs: 2 x A100. ETA ~8 min. Billing-bot: please pre-approve immediate burst for cedar-tenant-11 per contract override flow.

Billing-bot: Emergency burst pre-approved under contract CID-CE-778. Cost center charge will be routed to enterprise escalation bucket.

Maria (support): Notifying Cedar PM: "We are diverting traffic to a warm pool and enabling temporary burst capacity. You may see degraded latency and a small change in model responses while we stabilize. We will follow up with postmortem."

Ryan (acct): Cedar acknowledged and requested ETA to full restore. They asked us to prioritize minimal errors even if latency increases.

Alex (sre): throttling rule applied at edge: rate_limit=180 reqs/s per tenant (previously 600) for 10 minutes rolling window. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood/metrics/cedar/traffic.

Lina (eng-runtime): ran a quick health check on cedar-warm after diversion: return 200 on health ping, model version matches v2-q4, kv cache size 0 (will warm).

Sam (infra): emergency GPUs are up and attached to cedar-prod-d1-burst at 2165432410. Observed drop in queue length and 429s baseline decreasing.

Alex (sre): 429 rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in last 4 minutes. continuing monitoring.

Jay (oncall): handing off to next oncall @Sam in 20m. Sam please continue to own until we declare stable.

Sam (infra): taking ownership. I'll keep this thread updated and collect timeline for postmortem. Action items:
- Keep diversion in place 30m and monitor errors/latency
- Keep emergency burst for 1 hour, then scale down gradually
- Collect traffic profile and KV miss rate for Cedar for RCA
- Schedule postmortem with Eng + SRE + Account + Cedar team

Maria (support): Customer-facing note ready: "We applied a temporary routing and capacity increase for your traffic to prevent failures. We will share a detailed timeline and RCA within 48 hours." Sending now.

Alex (sre): marking incident as mitigated for immediate user-facing failures. Will leave thread open for followup.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED (P1 -> P2) at 2165432438.

Sam (infra): closing status update at 2165432445: 429s < 0.5%, latency within expected for fallback. Will start scale-down next check unless regressions. Postmortem owner: Alex + Lina.

Jay (oncall): thanks team. good coordination.
